text:
alex_frontend: quick heads-up — I ran `npm audit` against `console/ui` CI after the last merge and got a high severity finding for `source-map-resolve` (possible prototype pollution). Also noticed our Sentry uploads include `sourcesContent` in the sourcemaps, which could leak code paths. :eyes:

maria_sec: can you paste the audit output and the Sentry upload snippet? tagging @chris_build for pipeline/lockfile impact.

alex_frontend: here are the snippets:
```
$ npm audit --json | jq '.advisories["source-map-resolve"]'
{"findings":1, "severity":"high", "cves":["CVE-2025-34567"], "patched_versions":">=1.0.2"}
```
and our sourcemap upload in CI looks like:
```yaml
- name: Upload sourcemaps
  run: sentry-cli releases files $RELEASE upload-sourcemaps dist/js --rewrite --strip-prefix dist --include-sources
```
that `--include-sources` is what pulled sourcesContent into the map.

chris_build: thanks. two angles: 1) dependency fix and lockfile churn; 2) build config to avoid leaking source. For (1) we can bump `source-map-resolve` to patched version and run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` to update lock. For (2) remove `--include-sources` and re-upload maps.

jamie_pm: what's the risk to production? do we need an incident?

maria_sec: prototype pollution in a source-map resolver is bad because an attacker who can control map inputs could craft payloads that impact server-side tools that parse maps. For our frontend assets the primary risk is information disclosure (internal comments, file paths). Not a full RCE as far as I can tell. Prioritize as P2/P1? leaning P2 urgent fix with a patch release.

sec-bot: automated alert — CVE-2025-34567 affecting package `source-map-resolve` reported by OSS vulnerability feed. Recommended upgrade: >=1.0.2. See https://vuln-feed.example/CVE-2025-34567

alex_frontend: proposed remediation steps:
- drop `--include-sources` from CI upload (stop leaking sourcesContent)
- pin/upgrade `source-map-resolve` to >=1.0.2 in package-lock/pnpm-lock
- run `pnpm install` and open a PR with the lockfile update and a note about expected churn
- add CI regression check that ensures sourcemap files do not contain `sourcesContent`

chris_build: +1. for lock churn: we'll get changes across many transitive deps. Suggest we do the lock update in a short-lived branch and run the standard QA matrix. To reduce churn in monorepo, update only the vulnerable package with `pnpm up source-map-resolve@^1.0.2 --workspace-root` then `pnpm install --lockfile-only` and push the lockfile.

maria_sec: also add a short audit log entry and a ticket in security-triage with CVE id and timeline. I'll own post-merge verification and Sentry config review.

jamie_pm: timeline? can we get a patch out today?

alex_frontend: I can open the PR now. rough steps:
```bash
# update lock without changing local node_modules for devs
pnpm up source-map-resolve@^1.0.2 --workspace-root
pnpm install --lockfile-only
git add pnpm-lock.yaml
git commit -m "chore(ui): upgrade source-map-resolve to mitigate CVE-2025-34567"
git push origin fix/sourcemap-cve
```
I'll also change the deploy job to remove `--include-sources` in the same PR so we can validate in staging before prod.

chris_build: heads up — removing `--include-sources` means stack traces in Sentry will be less readable for devs. Workaround: keep source maps but strip `sourcesContent` and make sure sourcemaps are uploaded to a private Sentry release with access controls. We should add a short docs note.

maria_sec: agree. priority: 1) remove include-sources 2) upgrade package 3) verify no sourcesContent in uploaded maps 4) QA and deploy. Postmortem not required unless we find evidence of exploitation.

dependabot: I created a PR #1023 that bumps `source-map-resolve` to 1.0.2 and updates pnpm-lock. It includes the lockfile diff and a short CI run.

alex_frontend: saw #1023 — thanks. I'll add the CI change and the `sourcesContent` check to that branch.

chris_build: I'll prep a quick GH Action check to scan `.map` files for "sourcesContent" string and fail the job if present. Idea:
```yaml
- name: Ensure no sourcesContent in maps
  run: grep -R "\"sourcesContent\"" dist || exit 0  # fail only in release job
```
I'll add it to the release workflow.

maria_sec: once merged, I'll verify Sentry releases are re-uploaded without sources and will update the security ticket. After deploy we'll run `npm audit` again and confirm no remaining high findings.

jamie_pm: set expectation with eng leadership: patch rollout today, monitor tomorrow morning. update ops channel when prod deploy starts. :shipit:

alex_frontend: PR updated with the CI fix and build flag removed. ready for review @chris_build @maria_sec

chris_build: reviewing now. lockfile diff looks as expected (moderate churn). running CI locally.

sec-bot: vulnerability resolved in repo: `source-map-resolve` upgraded to 1.0.2 in branch fix/sourcemap-cve. CVE-2025-34567 marked fixed pending merge.

maria_sec: thanks all. leave this thread open until post-deploy verification completes.
